title: No bad restrictions with few free variables
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula in $n$ variables, and let $d$ and $s$ be natural numbers with $s \le d$. Then no restriction of the $n$ variables that leaves exactly $s$ variables free is bad for the Boolean function computed by $f$ at depth $d$; that is, the set of restrictions $\rho$ that both have exactly $s$ free variables and whose restricted function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$ is empty.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
ρ has exactly s free variables (IsRestriction s ρ)
ρ is bad for f.eval at depth d (restricted function has decision-tree depth > d)
conclusion: the filtered set of such restrictions is empty
replaced:
If $s \leq d$, the set of restrictions that are simultaneously $s$-restrictions
and bad restrictions for depth $d$ is empty.
